industry.size: Indian retail ~Rs68-72 trn in CY2023, projected Rs104-112 trn by CY2028 (~9% a year); organised retail Rs14.9 trn (CY2023) to Rs36-38 trn by CY2028 (~20% a year); unorganised still ~80% (AR FY26 MD&A, industry report; HSIE initiation 13-Apr-2026).
industry.valueRetail: Listed value retailers grew revenue ~25% y/y in Q1FY27 on ~20% area growth and ~5% sales per sq ft growth (MOSL sector note, 25-Sep-2026): V2 Retail +58% (73% area growth, 56 new stores in the quarter), V-Mart and Baazar Style Retail growing high-teens to 20s. VMM's 10% SSSG compares with 5.5% at DMart and ~7% at Reliance's big-box grocery (Emkay, 23-Jul-2026).
industry.dmartOverlap: VMM is strongest in the north and east (~63% of 793 stores at FY26); DMart in the west and south (~84% of its 500). Over half of DMart's stores are in towns of 1 mn+; VMM's core is the 50-250k population band (~39% of stores). In the west ~45% of VMM's 75 stores and in the south ~44% of its 217 stores are in towns with no DMart (HSIE initiation, 13-Apr-2026).
industry.quickCommerce: QC is a smaller threat in VMM's towns than in metros: VMM's own hyperlocal service reaches 767 stores; QC drives 6-8% of store revenue where organised competition is thin, 2-3% in crowded urban centres (HSIE). VMM's customers put absolute price ahead of convenience, and QC players lack VMM's own-brand SKUs.
industry.whitespace: HSIE maps ~1,246 more large-format stores (to ~2,039), 59% in the south and west; management (Sep-2026) speaks of ~1,200 more LFS plus ~4,000 small-format stores.
industry.src: AR FY26 MD&A; HSIE initiation (13-Apr-2026); MOSL value-fashion sector update (25-Sep-2026); Emkay result update (23-Jul-2026)

excluded.ABFRL: Loss-making in every year FY20-26 and restructured by the 2025 demerger of its lifestyle brands: no P/E history to compare.

peers.note: Retail peer set set by DMART.ctx.js (consumer-services batch; TRENT matches it): DMART, TRENT, METROBRAND, BATAINDIA, PAGEIND used; ABFRL and SHOPERSTOP excluded as stated; VMM excludes itself. VMM listed on 18-Dec-2024, so its own window is the 12 months from 1-Oct-2025 (the post-listing months to Sep-2025 skipped, PLAYBOOK §7c) and the sector move is measured over the same window: the used peers' trailing P/E at the 30-Sep-2026 close vs their own medians over Oct-2025 to Sep-2026 (HYUNDAI / BAJAJHFL / EMCURE precedent). The five-year move (DMART's -30% basis) is shown as a sensitivity row. Unlisted or uncovered value retailers (V2 Retail, V-Mart, Baazar Style) are not in the house peer set; MOSL's multiples for them are quoted in the text only.

street.note: Standing on 30-Sep-2026: the eight post-Q1FY27 notes with dated, named targets (MOSL, Emkay, ICICI Securities, Aditya Birla Money, Elara, Jefferies, Morgan Stanley, HSIE); all Buy/Overweight. Pre-Q1 notes are shown for method only. ICICI Securities' Oct-2026 note and any post-30-Sep changes are excluded.
street.methodSummary: Where the method is visible, brokers translate their targets into one-year-forward P/E: Emkay 55x Jun-28E EPS; HSIE DCF = ~44x Sep-28E EPS; MOSL DCF = ~34x Sep-28E pre-Ind AS EV/EBITDA, ~51x Sep-28E EPS. P/E on Sep-28E EPS is therefore our primary method; EV/EBITDA and DCF are cross-checks.

moat.cost: Lowest retailing cost per sq ft among value retailers (FY25 Rs1,794/sq ft, 19.4% of revenue, vs V-Mart Rs2,406 and DMart Rs2,370; HSIE); leased stores keep capital light (cash capex ~2.5% of revenue).
moat.brands: 74% own brands; FMCG own brands 30-50% cheaper than market leaders and ~10pp better margin; management holds the discount to leaders at least constant through inflation.
moat.reach: 819 stores in 559 cities (Jun-2026), ~74% in Tier 2 and smaller towns; loyalty base 175 mn (~95% of revenue).
moat.weakness: No pricing power by design (gains are reinvested); apparel competition (Zudio, V2, V-Mart, Style Bazaar) in the same towns; rents and minimum wages rise every year.

critiques: Bulls (Emkay, MOSL, Jefferies): double-digit SSSG with volume-led growth, a 2,000+ store runway and the lowest cost base in value retail justify 50x+ P/E on Sep/Jun-28E.
Cautious (HSIE): models only ~8% SSSG; the ~40% PE stake (two blocks in nine months) is a medium-term supply overhang; CEO is 65 and succession matters.

Our critique: the stock de-rated from the high 60s to the high 30s on one-year-forward EPS over the last 12 months without an earnings miss; the overhang and the market's retail de-rating, not the business, set the multiple.
governance: PE-controlled (Kedaara Capital and Partners Group via Samayat, 40.1%), professional management, independent chair; FPI cap of 49.99% proposed to keep Airplaza Indian-owned-and-controlled; promoter entity provides transport and warehousing (Rs103 cr in FY26).
